To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proteome of the honey bee worker larval development is characterized by a high number of proteins related to the nutrient metabolism and energy production.
(a) the proteome complement in honey bee larvae changes during the larval development and (b) the proteome of high royal jelly yielding larvae differs from that of low royal jelly yielding larvae.

1) the proteome of honey bees is highly dynamic, 2) the proteome complement changes significantly throughout development, 3) the proteome composition differs between strains of honey bees, 4) the proteome changes in a strain-specific manner during larval development.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterization of the proteome of worker honey bees during larval development in the context of a high royal jelly producing strain of Apis mel- lifera L., using two-dimensional gel electrophoresi, mass spectrometric analysis and bioinformatic tools.
the proteome of high royal jelly-producing bees (Apis mellifica L.) during worker bee larval development.
the identification of the proteome of worker bees of Apis melllifera L., which have been artificially selected for increased production of royal jelly, during the larval development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study provides an overview of the proteome of the honey bee during larval development.
the protein expression pattern during larval development is complex, and the identified proteins are related to the metabolism, growth and energy production of the larva.
the proteome of high royal jelly yielding bees is a complex mixture of proteins that are involved in larval nutrition, energy production and utilization and cell cycle regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the honey bee proteomics is still in its early stages.
the larval development of the honey bee is an energy dependent process, which is accompanied by a high level of protein expression.
the proteome complement in the larval development of the honeybee is a dynamic system, which is characterized by a variety of proteins with different functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the larval development of high royal jelly yielding bees is characterized by an increase in the expression of proteins involved in energy metabolism, amino acid metabolism, and the cell cycle, as well as by the persistence of proteins involved in protein folding, DNA repair, and fatty acid metabolism, respectively.

we have shown that the larval proteome is dynamic and that the expression of proteins involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates and amino acids, the energy metabolism, the cell cycle and the larval development itself is changing during development.
the proteome of developing honeybee larvae is a complex and dynamic system.
